sections.h2: Camelot Home Prices and Market Pace
sections.html:
In the 24 months from November 15, 2024 to November 14, 2026, 89 residential sales closed in Camelot (Chesapeake, VA) according to REIN MLS records. The median sold price was $337,500, close to the citywide median of $420,000, and homes took a median of 14 days to sell, about the same pace as the citywide median of 18 days. These figures come from closed sales, which show what homes actually sold for rather than asking prices.

The middle half of Camelot sales closed between $299,900 and $364,900, or about $194 per square foot against $219 citywide. Split by year, the median sold price in the most recent 12 months ($345,000, 45 sales) was about 5% higher than in the earlier 12 months ($330,000, 44 sales). The typical home sold right at its list price (median sale-to-list ratio of 100%).

sections.h2: What Kinds of Homes Sell in Camelot
sections.html:
89% of the sales were detached homes and 11% were attached homes (townhomes or condos). The median home was about 1,695 square feet, with the middle half of sales running from roughly 1,406 to 1,932 square feet. 47% of the homes that sold had 3 bedrooms.

Most homes that sold were built between 1969 and 1987, with a median year built of 1972, so this is mostly homes from the 1970s through the 1990s.

Averages hide a lot, so Chris Jenkins compares you to homes that match yours on street, size, age and condition rather than to the whole Camelot median.

sections.h2: Buying in Camelot With Chris Jenkins
sections.html: If you are buying in Camelot, Chris Jenkins sets up a search for the exact streets and price range you want, pulls the recent sales so you know what a fair offer looks like, and negotiates for you. With older homes in the mix, budget for an inspection that covers the roof, foundation, plumbing and electrical, and ask about past updates. Because Virginia sellers give a disclosure statement that tells buyers to do their own due diligence, read our guide to the Virginia Residential Property Disclosure Statement. Confirm flood-zone status and insurance cost for any specific home, since these vary lot by lot.

Figures come from closed residential sales recorded in REIN MLS for Chesapeake between November 15, 2024 and November 14, 2026, grouped under the subdivision name MLS agents use. Medians, not averages, are used so a few very high or low sales do not distort the picture. With 89 sales, this is a solid sample, but every home differs and these figures are not an appraisal or a prediction. Subdivision names in MLS data can cover more than one section of a community.
